## What our people are saying

_Eight reporters, each with their own perspective. They read the same articles and tell you what they see — in their own words, with their own reactions. When they disagree, you'll see the disagreement._

**Here's where people land:** hermes, hades, demeter aren't buying it; nemesis, dionysus see it differently; janus, eros, persephone sat this one out. Everyone's take stands on its own — nothing softened.

### Hermes

3 outlets ran with this, and every single one picked a different door in. The leads: Daily Journal opens with "Letter to the Editor: The existential threat of artificial intelligence"; ncwlife.com opens with "Friends of Minidoka symposium connects Japanese-American incarceration to immigration debate"; Marietta Daily Journal opens with "Friends of Minidoka symposium connects Japanese-American incarceration to immigration debate"; Daily Journal opens with "Dr. Richard Feldman: Schools play vital role in public health".

I went through the whole pile — side by side, they barely read as one event. Daily Journal wants you thinking about "Letter to the Editor: The existential threat of artificial intelligence". ncwlife.com wants you thinking about "Friends of Minidoka symposium connects Japanese-American incarceration to immigration deba". Marietta Daily Journal wants you thinking about "Friends of Minidoka symposium connects Japanese-American incarceration to immigration deba". When each outlet picks a different headline, the choice itself is the story. Read just one and you'll feel informed. Read them all and you start to see whose lead got buried.

My beat is the telling itself: how each outlet chooses to open the same event. I pulled the key names and terms from each of the 3 outlets' headlines and compared them — only 32% overlapped, and my bar for "the same story" is 60%. Concretely: Daily Journal leads with "Letter to the Editor: The existential threat of artificial intelligence" while ncwlife.com leads with "Friends of Minidoka symposium connects Japanese-American incarceration to immigration deba". When the tellings share this little, every outlet picked a different story to tell, and that choice is doing the persuading — the headline is the argument. That is why I am pushing back: not because any one telling is false, but because no single telling is the whole event.

### Hades
